content:
# Sirach 33 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** SIR 033 | **Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Total Disagreements:** 17

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.2: "hate the law" vs. "embrace God's instruction"

- **EMET/LOGOS:** "A wise man will not hate the law"
- **PNEUMA:** "A wise person embraces God's instruction"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "will not hate the law" — the negative formulation is Ben Sira's; PNEUMA converts it to a positive without warrant and loses the force of "hate" (μισήσει).

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2b: "boat in a storm" vs. "ship in a storm"

- **EMET:** "like a boat in a storm"
- **LOGOS:** "like a ship in a storm"
- **PNEUMA:** "like a ship caught in a storm"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "like a ship in a storm" — πλοῖον can be either; "ship" suggests more dramatic scale; PNEUMA adds "caught" without warrant.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: "as when inquiring by Urim" vs. "as a divine oracle"

- **EMET:** "as when inquiring by Urim"
- **LOGOS:** "as reliable as a divine oracle"
- **PNEUMA:** "as reliable as a sacred oracle"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "as reliable as a divine oracle" — EMET's Urim reference is a legitimate interpretation but may be too specific for the Greek text; LOGOS's rendering is clear without being vague.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.5: "cartwheel" vs. "wagon wheel"

- **EMET/PNEUMA:** "cartwheel"
- **LOGOS:** "wagon wheel"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "cartwheel" — more vivid and common in English; both render τροχός correctly.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.6: "mocking friend" vs. "sarcastic friend"

- **EMET:** "a mocking friend"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "a sarcastic friend"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "a sarcastic friend" — the verb implies cutting mockery; "mocking" is accurate but "sarcastic" captures the social dynamic better.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.8: source of distinction

- **EMET:** "By the Lord's decision they were distinguished"
- **LOGOS:** "by the knowledge of the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "The Lord in his wisdom"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "by the Lord's wisdom" — ἐν γνώσει κυρίου; LOGOS's "knowledge" is accurate; "wisdom" (PNEUMA) captures the sense well. Combined: "distinguished by the Lord's wisdom."

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.12: three-part distinction of human fates

- **EMET:** "blessed and exalted...cursed and humbled, and turned them out"
- **LOGOS:** "blessed and exalted...cursed and humbled and removed from their station"
- **PNEUMA:** "blessed and lifted high...cursed and lowered, uprooting them"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** LOGOS's "removed from their station" is more precise than EMET's "turned out" and more dignified than PNEUMA's "uprooting."

---

## Disagreement 8 — v.13: "all his ways are as he pleases" vs. "to be shaped in whatever way he pleases"

- **EMET:** "for all his ways are as he pleases"
- **LOGOS:** "to be shaped in whatever way he pleases"
- **PNEUMA:** "shaped however the potter pleases"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "to be shaped in whatever way he pleases" — LOGOS keeps the clay-shaping metaphor active throughout the verse.

---

## Disagreement 9 — v.14: "opposite" vs. "counterpart"

- **EMET:** "Good is the opposite of evil"
- **LOGOS:** "Good is the counterpart of evil"
- **PNEUMA:** "Good and evil are opposites"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "counterpart" — ἀντίκειμαι means "set against" or "opposed"; "counterpart" captures the paired-creation theology better than the blunt "opposite," which sounds merely logical rather than cosmological.

---

## Disagreement 10 — v.16: "last to keep watch" vs. "came along last"

- **EMET:** "I myself was the last to keep watch"
- **LOGOS:** "I too was the last to wake up"
- **PNEUMA:** "I myself came along last"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "I too was the last to keep watch" — ἠγρύπνησα means "I was wakeful/watchful"; LOGOS's "wake up" is imprecise; PNEUMA loses the image of vigilance entirely.

---

## Disagreement 11 — v.19: giving authority away

- **EMET:** "give no power over yourself...give not your goods to another"
- **LOGOS:** "do not give authority over yourself...do not give your property to another"
- **PNEUMA:** "do not hand over your authority...don't give away your property"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** LOGOS's rendering is most precise; "property" is better than "goods" (EMET) for the broader term κτήματα.

---

## Disagreement 12 — v.21: "look to the hands of your sons" vs. "dependent on them"

- **EMET:** "look to the hands of your sons"
- **LOGOS:** "look expectantly at the hands of your sons"
- **PNEUMA:** "dependent on them"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "look expectantly toward the hands of your sons" — the idiom of watching someone's hands for food/help is biblical and should be preserved; PNEUMA flattens it.

---

## Disagreement 13 — v.22: "bring no blot" vs. "let no blot come"

- **EMET:** "bring no blot upon your glory"
- **LOGOS:** "let no one bring a stain upon your honor"
- **PNEUMA:** "don't let anyone tarnish your reputation"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "let no blot come upon your honor" — "honor" (LOGOS) fits better than "glory" (EMET) in this domestic context; PNEUMA is accurate but loses the blot/stain imagery.

---

## Disagreement 14 — v.24: "servant" vs. "slave"

- **EMET/PNEUMA:** "servant"
- **LOGOS:** "slave"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "servant" — δοῦλος can mean either; the broader context (vv. 25–31) suggests a household slave, but "servant" is the more common English rendering in wisdom literature contexts and avoids importing anachronistic moral weight.

---

## Disagreement 15 — v.25: "seek liberty" vs. "seek his freedom"

- **EMET:** "he will seek liberty"
- **LOGOS:** "he will seek his freedom"
- **PNEUMA:** "he'll start thinking about freedom"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "he will seek his freedom" — direct and clear; PNEUMA's "thinking about" weakens the action implied in the Greek.

---

## Disagreement 16 — v.30: "treat him as a brother" vs. "treat him as yourself"

- **EMET:** "treat him as a brother"
- **LOGOS:** "let him be to you like yourself"
- **PNEUMA:** "treat him like a member of the family"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "treat him as yourself" — ὡς ψυχήν σου lit. "as your own soul"; EMET's "brother" is an interpretation; PNEUMA's "family" is too free.

---

## Disagreement 17 — v.30b: "you have need of him" vs. "you've paid good money"

- **EMET:** "for as your own soul you have need of him"
- **LOGOS:** "because you have acquired him by blood"
- **PNEUMA:** "after all, you've paid good money for him"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "for you have need of him as of your own life" — the point is mutual dependence, not financial transaction; PNEUMA's rendering reduces the relationship to commerce.
